entries.title: Ezekiel 3:1
segments: Eat this roll; this symbol denotes the inward willing reception of the prophetical messages committed to him.  Compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:3
segments: As honey for sweetness; he received the divine revelations with holy delight, although their contents of "lamentations, and mourning, and woe" were bitter to him.  Compare

. 
 
That we may be prepared to proclaim God's truth to others, we must first receive it with holy obedience and joy into our own hearts, and make it our daily food and strength.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:5
segments:
Of a strange speech--a hard language; that is, speaking a foreign tongue unintelligible to him. 
 
In the work of making known God's truth to our own neighbors and countrymen we enjoy many advantages above the foreign missionary, who goes to people of strange customs and a strange speech; these advantages ought to excite us to great zeal and diligence in the performance of this duty.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:6
segments:
. 
 
vv 6-7. 
 
None are so hardhearted and desperately wicked as those who have enjoyed and abused great religious privileges.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:8
segments:
vv 8-9. 
 
When God appoints his servants to any work, he gives them the strength and grace which they need for its performance.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:12
segments: Took me up; "lifted me up between the earth and the heaven," and took me away to Tel-abib; compare
and 8.3.  This, however, was not bodily, but in prophetic vision; for he afterwards went thither by his own proper act, as is plain from

. The vision indicated a duty which he immediately performed. 
 
  A voice of a great rushing; the sound of the cherubim and wheels in motion, for "whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went."

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:13
segments: The noise of the wings; compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:14
segments:
I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit; full of grief and holy anger.  The spirit of prophecy brought his feelings towards his countrymen into harmony with those of God. 
 
A burning zeal for the glory of God, united with "great heaviness" of heart in view of men's perverseness and rebellion, have been in all ages the marks of God's true servants.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:15
segments:
Astonished; in view of the solemn office committed to me. 
 
Silent meditation and prayer are among the best means of preparation for a great and difficult service.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:16
segments: At the end of seven days; Ezekiel, like Saul of Tarsus, was left, for a period after his call, to his own meditations.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:17
segments:
vv 17-21. 
 
God holds the preacher responsible for the faithful delivery of his messages: when this is done, it is both the preacher's duty and his privilege to leave the consequences with God.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:20
segments: A stumbling-block; any occasion of sin which comes to men through God's providence for their trial.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:25
segments: They shall put bands upon thee; that is, thou shalt be bound at my command.  This is probably to be understood figuratively of a divine restraint at certain times from the exercise of the prophetical office, as is explained in the following verses.

entries.title: Ezekiel 3:26
segments:
vv 26-27. 
 
  Will make thy tongue cleave--when I speak; he is to keep silence, except when God's Spirit moves him to speak; the perverseness of he people makes this reserve necessary. 
 
God sometimes, in his displeasure, withdraws his admonitions from the perverse and incorrigible, and leaves them to their own ways.
